About System Designer

System Designer is a free browser game for learning system design. I'm Aditya Reddy and I built it.

Build your first system
Who makes it

What the game is

Each problem is a kind of system people actually run (a URL shortener, a bank ledger, a concert ticket drop etc). Read the brief and the answers to its questions, work out the numbers, then drag parts onto the canvas and connect them. Once you press Start the clock runs from 00:00 to 24:00 and the day's traffic goes through your design, viral spikes, outages and retry storms included. The debrief after that is in plain words. It shows reliability, speed, data safety and monthly cost, and which event hurt.

Right now there are 82 problems across 15 industries, and 41 lessons that take one idea at a time. Challenge gives everyone the same seeded scenario each day. Sandbox has no score, so any part, any traffic, any event. Medium and Hard problems also have Interview mode, a timed discussion where you defend what you picked with evidence.

Prices are rounded from the big cloud providers' public list prices, and capacities and latencies from commonly published figures. Treat them as a sense of scale.

How it gets updated

Everything is in one public GitHub repository, the game, these pages and the sign-in service. I merge a change into main and Cloudflare Pages deploys it. The problem, lesson and guide pages get generated from the same content the game plays, so when a problem changes its page changes with it.

I measured each problem's budget and targets by playing its reference design through a full simulated day, and the checks in the repo replay all of them. Every change is in the commit history. The sitemap has the date each page last changed.

Accounts and email

Since November 20, 2026 there's no account or email needed to play, that covers every lesson, problem, the daily challenge and the sandbox. Progress stays in your browser. Sign in with Google or GitHub only if you want progress synced across devices or a score on a Challenge leaderboard.

Problem pages are open. Guide and lesson pages show the intro and then ask for an email to read the rest (weekly update emails are a separate tick box, and it starts unticked). What's stored and how to delete it is on the privacy page.

Feedback and fixes

If a number looks off or something breaks, open an issue on GitHub with the page and the steps to get there. There's also a feedback form in Settings. Fixes to problem and lesson text are welcome, the contributor guide has the checks to run.
